title: Quotations on Tokugawa money, the Dojima rice market and silver and copper in Qing China (Chapter 17)
source: 清史稿 (卷一百二十四、一百二十五); 盛康编《皇朝经世文续编》(卷三十一、五十八) and 葛士浚编《皇朝经世文续编》(卷七十八、八十五), from the daizhigev20 corpus; Suzuki (2021); Schaede (1989); Takatsuki (2007); Irigoin (2013); MLIT (2011); Atwell (2008), a review of Lin (2006)
series: one row per quoted fact: id, dynasty (country or dynasty), year (approximate where year_note says so), year_note, value (several values separated by ';'), unit, numeral (for corpus rows: the classical numeral read by classical_numerals.py, compared with the first value), file (a corpus key of verify_quotes.py or a key of sources below), juan (卷 and piece for corpus rows; page, note or table otherwise), quote (verbatim), note
license: Short quotations only, for comment and teaching. The Qing texts are in the public domain; the modern research is quoted, not copied.
fetch: data/fetch/verify_quotes.py (corpus rows) and data/fetch/verify_web_quotes.py (rows citing the sources below)
notes: Corpus rows (files qingshigao, huangchaojingshiwenxubian = 盛康's 续编, huangchaojingshiwenxubian_ge = 葛士浚's 续编) are checked against daizhigev20 at commit 4a6d6f2 by verify_quotes.py; rows citing suzuki2021, schaede1989, takatsuki2007, irigoin2013, atwell2008 and mlit2011 against the downloaded PDFs by verify_web_quotes.py; rows citing suzuki2021img were read on the page images and are counted but not checked by a script. Second versions: the 清史稿 rows were compared with the Wikisource text of 卷124 and 卷125 (traditional characters; 准 for 準 as in the corpus); 包世臣's 银荒小补说 with the Wikisource text of 《齐民四术》 卷二 (it reads 一千八百八十五文 where the 续编 has 一千八百八十余文 in the second mention, and 老幼通知 for 老幼皆知); 林则徐's passage also appears in 《皇朝经世文统编》 in the corpus; 曾国藩's 拟银钱并用章程疏 also in 《皇朝经世文四编》. 曾国藩's 备陈民间疾苦疏, 吴嘉宾's and 周腾虎's pieces were found in one edition only. The corpus punctuates 刘良驹's sentence as '几及二千文外。省则', which should read '几及二千文。外省则'; the chapter uses the corrected punctuation. Dates: 吴嘉宾 dates 刘良驹's memorial to 道光乙巳 (1845); 曾国藩 names the memorials of 道光二十四、二十五、二十六年 (1844-1846) as earlier, and his 备陈民间疾苦疏 says that since 道光十六年 (1836) 江苏 has reported shortfalls every year; the corpus gives neither memorial a date, so the year column gives the lower bound the texts imply (1836 for 备陈民间疾苦疏, which says 自十六年至今 and was written while 曾国藩 was at the Board of Punishments, 臣在刑部; 1846 for 拟银钱并用章程疏). Suzuki's Table 2 gives Keicho koban 84.291 per cent gold and 17.85 g, Genroku 57.366 per cent and 17.85 g, so the pure gold fell by 31.94 per cent (her text: 31.91); Kyoho 86.785 per cent and 17.85 g against Genbun 65.714 per cent and 13.13 g, a fall of 44.30 per cent (her text: 44.34). Her pure-gold figures in the Echigoya example (8.581726 g per Genbun koban, 11.9759232 g for 0.8 ryo of Keicho) imply weights of about 13.06 g and 17.76 g, not the table's 13.13 and 17.85. Arai's reminting figures give 13,236,534/8,824,350 = 1.500 new ryo per old ryo against a pure-gold ratio of 84.291/57.366 = 1.469; for silver 357,535.380/287,617.155 = 1.243 against 80/64 = 1.25. The mint officer's totals (20,000,000 ryo; 400,000 kan) mean that 44 per cent of the gold and 72 per cent of the silver were reminted; Suzuki summarizes this as 'broadly ... half'. Schaede's 200 monme per koku in 1714 and about 30 in 1718 (from Sugie 1984) do not match Iwahashi's annual Osaka prices (149.2 in 1714, 127.9 in 1718, 40.6 in 1719; snapshot gpih_iwahashi_rice); the chapter uses Iwahashi. Translations into Chinese in the chapter are the book's own.
